citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team (2025). ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv:2507.04952.
creator: Chenchen Zhang, Yuhang Li, Can Xu, Jiaheng Liu, Ao Liu, Changzhi Zhou, Ken Deng, Dengpeng Wu, Guanhua Huang, Kejiao Li, Qi Yi, Ruibin Xiong, Shihui Hu, Yue Zhang, Yuhao Jiang, Zenan Xu, Yuanxing Zhang, Wiggin Zhou, Chayse Zhou, Fengzong Lian (Tencent Hunyuan Team)
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark of 1,825 diverse tasks for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual code generation. It covers nine domains (Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications, Simulations, Data Science, Management Systems, Multimedia Editing, Quick Tools, and Others), stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers. The benchmark is paired with an automated, multimodal evaluation pipeline that renders artifacts, captures three-step temporal screenshots, and uses a checklist-guided MLLM-as-Judge to assess visual fidelity, interactive correctness, and code quality.
name: ArtifactsBench
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each query is paired with one 10-dimension checklist. Human validation used multiple annotators per item (median of individual annotators' ratings used as ground truth), but the exact number of annotators per item is not specified.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human validators in the 280-instance expert study were described as engineers with extensive front-end development experience. No further demographic details (nationality, age, gender) are provided.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement on the 10% manually curated checklist seed achieved Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators. A 280-instance double-blind human expert study (6 models, multiple front-end engineers) measured pairwise consistency (Pair ACC) between the automated MLLM referee and human judges, achieving up to 90.95% pairwise agreement with Gemini-2.5-Pro as referee.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom internal pipeline; checklist generation used Hunyuan-Turbos (LLM-drafted) followed by human refinement. Automated evaluation used headless Chromium (Playwright) for artifact execution and screenshot capture.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were LLM-drafted (using Hunyuan-Turbos) and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators; the seed is reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent. Solvability validation collected candidate solutions from multiple model families and pruned underspecified items. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark explicitly controls for contamination and near-duplicate content via two-stage de-duplication (MinHash + semantic similarity and perceptual hashing). License-violating items were filtered out during sourcing. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks (e.g., hard-coded coordinates that break under minor viewport changes) were revised or removed to avoid rewarding non-generalizable solutions. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated model performance rather than a priori to preserve discriminative power and avoid calibration bias.
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). The curated pool was then seeded for further expansion via prompt rewriting and difficulty calibration.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw sources include expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and screenshots used for LLM visual-to-query generation.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation of dynamic behavior relies on discrete screenshot sampling at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions (e.g., multi-step user workflows, nuanced physics in games). The benchmark evaluates only single-turn artifact generation and does not assess agentic, iterative, or multi-turn development capabilities. Future work is needed for richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots and broader artifact domains.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce a 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split (realized as 559/611/655). Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks. Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities, LLM-drafted and then human-refined. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration (Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators) and was reused as few-shot references.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Two-stage de-duplication was applied: (i) MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified the results.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings. Future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ArtifactsBench provides a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models, enabling more reliable automated evaluation of LLM-generated interactive visual artifacts. By aligning automated evaluation with human preferences (94.4% ranking consistency with WebDev Arena), it reduces reliance on costly manual evaluation and supports broader community access to reproducible benchmarking.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLMs on their ability to generate high-quality, interactive visual artifacts (web widgets, data visualizations, mini-games, SVG graphics, simulations, management systems) from multimodal instructions. Benchmarking and comparing 30+ LLMs on visual fidelity, interactive correctness, and code quality. Providing fine-grained diagnostic insights into model strengths and failure modes for user-centric generative model development.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos (used to LLM-draft checklists); Gemini-2.5-Pro (used as MLLM-as-Judge referee for automated scoring and query classification); Qwen2.5-VL-72B (used as open-source MLLM-as-Judge referee); GPT-o4-mini (used in ablation studies as referee); lightweight classifier for sub-category tagging; MinHash for semantic de-duplication; perceptual hashing for visual de-duplication; Playwright/headless Chromium for artifact execution and screenshot capture.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific data collection timeframe (start/end dates or period) is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the collection process; incomplete items were simply filtered out rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; incomplete or non-visual items were discarded rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of code generation tasks/prompts and does not collect personal or sensitive information. The quality filtering prompt explicitly checks for privacy (avoiding sensitive personal information), confirming no PII is included.
null_reasons.license: No license is explicitly stated in the paper; the paper only says it is open-sourced.
